items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Dark Church, the Buckle Church and the Apple Church. Then look for the Snake Church, and end your walk at the Nunnery.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the Dark Church, the Buckle Church and the Apple Church. Then look for the Snake Church, and end your walk at the Nunnery.

items.text: Did you know? The frescoes of the Dark Church emerged from a restoration that took ten years to lift away the soot, and the intensity of their blue is unmatched in the Byzantine world. The church takes its name from its single small window: because so little light gets in, its frescoes are the most vividly coloured in Cappadocia. Here is another curiosity. Most of the rock churches were carved with columns and arches that hold nothing up. Inside solid rock they serve no structural purpose at all; they are there so that the space would look like a real church. And one last detail: the blue of the Buckle Church was made from lapis lazuli, which at the time was more expensive than gold.

items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Freilichtmuseum Göreme in der Provinz Nevşehir. Epoche: 10.–12. Jahrhundert nach Christus Eine Gruppe von Klöstern und Kirchen, in den Tuff gehauen; die Fresken der Dunklen Kirche gehören zu den am besten erhaltenen byzantinischen Malereien überhaupt.

items.text: Vulkanischer Tuff ist weich genug, um ihn mit der Spitzhacke abzutragen, und härtet aus, sobald er geschnitten ist; deshalb wurde das Tal von Göreme ab dem zehnten Jahrhundert zu einer Landschaft der Klöster: Kirchen, Refektorien und Zellen wurden eine nach der anderen ausgehöhlt. Manche wurden auf Putz bemalt, andere direkt auf den Fels; die Dunkle Kirche hat ihre Farben bewahrt, weil nur ein einziges kleines Fenster Licht hereinlässt.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Fresken der Dunklen Kirche kamen bei einer Restaurierung zum Vorschein, die zehn Jahre dauerte, um den Ruß zu entfernen, und die Leuchtkraft ihres Blaus ist in der byzantinischen Welt unerreicht. Die Dunkle Kirche ist nach ihrem einzigen kleinen Fenster benannt: Weil so wenig Licht hereinfällt, sind ihre Fresken die farbenprächtigsten Kappadokiens. Die meisten Felskirchen wurden mit Säulen und Bögen gehauen, die nichts tragen. Im massiven Fels sind sie statisch sinnlos: Sie sind nur da, damit der Raum wie eine echte Kirche aussieht. Das Blau der Schnallenkirche wurde aus Lapislazuli gewonnen – damals teurer als Gold.

items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Музей под открытым небом Гёреме, провинция Невшехир. Период: X–XII века нашей эры Группа монастырей и церквей, высеченных в туфе; фрески Тёмной церкви, одни из наиболее сохранившихся византийских росписей в мире.

items.text: Вулканический туф достаточно мягок, чтобы копать его киркой, и твердеет после того, как его вырубят; вот почему долина Гёреме с десятого века превратилась в край монастырей: церкви, трапезные и кельи выдалбливали одну за другой. Одни расписывали по штукатурке, другие прямо по скале; Тёмная церковь сохранила свои краски, потому что свет в неё проникает лишь через одно маленькое окно.

items.text: А вы знали? Фрески Тёмной церкви открылись в ходе реставрации, на удаление копоти потребовалось десять лет, и насыщенность их синего цвета не имеет равных в византийском мире. Тёмная церковь названа так из-за единственного маленького окна: поскольку внутрь проникает так мало света, её фрески — самые яркие в Каппадокии. Большинство скальных церквей высечены с колоннами и арками, которые ничего не поддерживают. Внутри сплошной скалы они конструктивно бессмысленны: они нужны лишь для того, чтобы пространство выглядело как настоящая церковь. Синий цвет Церкви с пряжкой получали из лазурита — в то время он стоил дороже золота.

items.text: How do you build a city beneath the ground? Here, people sank a vertical shaft into soft tuff and cut rooms off it sideways. Eight levels can be walked, and the city is thought to run deeper still. Each level could be sealed from the inside with round stone doors weighing up to about a tonne, and the 55-metre ventilation shaft doubled as a well.
items.speech: How do you build a city beneath the ground? Here, people sank a vertical shaft into soft tuff and cut rooms off it sideways. Eight levels can be walked, and the city is thought to run deeper still. Each level could be sealed from the inside with round stone doors weighing up to about a tonne, and the 55-metre ventilation shaft doubled as a well.

items.text: As you make your way down, don't miss the ventilation shaft and the rolling stone doors. Look for the church and baptistery, and for the winery and the stables, too.
items.speech: As you make your way down, don't miss the ventilation shaft and the rolling stone doors. Look for the church and baptistery, and for the winery and the stables, too.

items.text: Did you know? The city came to light by accident in 1963. A householder knocked through a wall and found a room behind it, and behind that room, a whole underground city. The round stone doors between levels can weigh up to about a tonne and were designed to be opened only from the inside. And the 55-metre ventilation shaft also served as a well.

items.text: Ayaklarınızın altında bir kent var. Nevşehir'deki Kaymaklı Yeraltı Şehri'ne hoş geldiniz. Bu kaya yerleşiminin hikâyesi MÖ 1. binyıla uzanıyor; Bizans döneminde ise genişletildi. Derinkuyu'dan daha geniş ama tavanları daha alçak. Bugün dört katını gezebiliyorsunuz. Ve tüneller hâlâ yukarıdaki köy evlerinin altına uzanıyor.

Ve tüneller hâlâ yukarıdaki köy evlerinin altına uzanıyor.

items.text: Kaymaklı, Derinkuyu'ya göre daha yayvan ve daha alçak tavanlıdır. Koridorlarında eğilerek yürüyeceksiniz; o kadar darlar. Odalar bir avlunun çevresinde kümelenmiş. Her kümenin kendi mutfağı, kendi deposu var; yani her biri ayrı bir hane gibi düzenlenmiş. Ve yukarıda, yüzeyde, köyün evleri hâlâ bu tünellerin üstünde duruyor; bazıları depo olarak kullanılmayı sürdürüyor.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Kaymaklı ile Derinkuyu arasında dokuz kilometrelik bir tünel olduğu söylenir. Bu iddia kanıtlanmadı; ama iki kent arasındaki galeriler hâlâ tam olarak haritalanmış değil. Koridorların alçak ve dar olması da tesadüf değil: içeri girmek zorunda kalan bir saldırgan eğilmek ve tek sıra ilerlemek zorundaydı. Ve yukarıdaki köyün evleri hâlâ bu tünellerin üzerinde duruyor; köylüler bir bölümünü bugün de depo olarak kullanıyor.

items.text: Mind your head. You are entering Kaymaklı Underground City, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province dating from the 1st millennium BC and extended under Byzantium. It is wider and lower-ceilinged than Derinkuyu, with four levels open to visitors, and its tunnels still run beneath the village houses above.
items.speech: Mind your head. You are entering Kaymaklı Underground City, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province dating from the 1st millennium BC and extended under Byzantium. items.text: Kaymaklı is broader and lower than Derinkuyu, and its corridors are narrow enough that you have to stoop. Notice how the rooms cluster around courtyards. Each cluster is laid out like a separate household, with its own kitchen and stores. And life still goes on above you: the village stands on these tunnels, and some of them are still used for storage.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the stables and the church, then the stores and kitchens. Look for the basalt workshop stone, and glance up at the ventilation shafts.

items.text: Did you know? A nine-kilometre tunnel is said to link Kaymaklı to Derinkuyu. The claim is unproven, but the galleries between the two have never been fully mapped. The corridors were made low and narrow on purpose: an attacker who got in had to stoop, and go single file. And the village above still stands on these tunnels, its people still using parts of them for storage.

Bir vadide kaya kiliseleri, ötekinde kayaya oyulmuş bir cami. Peki bu hayat nasıl sona erdi? 1950'lerde kayalar çatlamaya, çökmeye başladı. Köy boşaltıldı ve halk iki kilometre ötedeki Yeni Zelve'ye taşındı.

items.text: Zelve Open Air Museum, in Nevşehir province, is a rock settlement whose story runs from the 9th century AD to 1952. Spread over three valleys, it was lived in without a break until 1952, when the danger of collapse emptied it.
items.speech: Zelve Open Air Museum, in Nevşehir province, is a rock settlement whose story runs from the 9th century AD to 1952. Spread over three valleys, it was lived in without a break until 1952, when the danger of collapse emptied it.

items.text: Spread over three valleys, Zelve was one of the places where Cappadocia's Christian and Muslim inhabitants lived side by side in the same rock: rock-cut churches in one valley, a rock-cut mosque in another. Then, in the 1950s, the cliffs began to crack and fall, and the village was evacuated to New Zelve, two kilometres away.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Fish Church and the Grape Church, then the Rock-cut mosque. Look out, too, for the Mill and the Tunnels.

items.text: Did you know? Zelve is one of the few Cappadocian settlements whose abandonment has an exact date: the village was cleared in 1952, so some of the people who lived in it are still alive. It is also one of the few places where a rock-cut church and a rock-cut mosque stand side by side in the same cliff. And why was it left? Because the rock was starting to collapse.

items.text: Melendiz Çayı'nın 100 metre derinliğinde oyduğu bir kanyondasınız. Burası Aksaray'daki Ihlara Vadisi, bir kaya yerleşimi. Dönemi MS 9-11. yüzyıl. Duvarlarında freskli onlarca kaya kilisesi saklı; birazdan onların izini süreceğiz.
items.speech: Melendiz Çayı'nın 100 metre derinliğinde oyduğu bir kanyondasınız. Burası Aksaray'daki Ihlara Vadisi, bir kaya yerleşimi. Dönemi milattan sonra 9 ile 11. yüzyıl. Duvarlarında freskli onlarca kaya kilisesi saklı; birazdan onların izini süreceğiz.

items.text: Her şey bir çayla başladı. Melendiz Çayı, volkanik platoyu on dört kilometre boyunca yüz metre derinliğinde yararak bu dar kanyonu açtı. Bizans döneminde vadinin dik duvarlarına yüzden fazla kilise ve şapel oyuldu. Fresklere bakarsanız iki ayrı dünya görürsünüz: Kapadokya'nın yerel, Doğu etkili resmi ile İstanbul'dan gelen Bizans saray üslubu. İkisi de aynı vadide, yan yana duruyor.

Vadi 14 kilometre uzunluğunda, yer yer 100 metre derinliğindedir; duvarlarına yüzden fazla kilise ve şapel oyulmuştur. Freskler ise iki ayrı dünyanın resmini bir arada gösterir: yerel Kapadokya üslubu Doğu etkisi taşırken, aynı vadideki bazı kiliseler İstanbul saray üslubuyla boyanmıştır.

items.text: Look down. Before you opens Ihlara Valley, a rock settlement in Aksaray province, from the 9th–11th century AD. It is a canyon cut 100 metres deep by the Melendiz river, and its walls are honeycombed with frescoed rock churches.
items.speech: Look down. Before you opens Ihlara Valley, a rock settlement in Aksaray province, from the 9th–11th century AD. It is a canyon cut 100 metres deep by the Melendiz river, and its walls are honeycombed with frescoed rock churches.

items.text: Patiently, the Melendiz river cut a fourteen-kilometre gorge a hundred metres deep into the volcanic plateau. In the Byzantine period, more than a hundred churches and chapels were carved into its walls. Their frescoes fall into two styles: the local Cappadocian manner, with its eastern influence, and the court style of Constantinople. Two worlds, standing side by side in one valley.

items.text: Did you know? More than three hundred steps lead down into the gorge, and its floor stays markedly cooler than the plateau in summer — one reason monastic life favoured it. The valley runs fourteen kilometres and reaches a hundred metres deep, with more than a hundred churches and chapels cut into its walls. And the frescoes hold two worlds together: the local Cappadocian manner shows eastern influence, while other churches in the same valley are painted in the court style of Constantinople.

items.text: Look up. Sumela Monastery, in Trabzon province, clings to a 300-metre cliff above the Altındere valley. Its story begins in the 4th century AD, and at its heart lies a rock church covered with frescoes, inside and out.
items.speech: Look up. Sumela Monastery, in Trabzon province, clings to a 300-metre cliff above the Altındere valley. Its story begins in the 4th century AD, and at its heart lies a rock church covered with frescoes, inside and out.

items.text: The monastery was founded in the fourth century, but it owes most of its present form to the thirteenth, under the Empire of Trebizond. It began as a natural cave turned into a church, and over the centuries it grew into a five-storey complex. Ottoman sultans confirmed its privileges by decree. Then, in the population exchange of 1923, it was emptied.

items.text: Did you know? The outer wall of the rock church is frescoed too. The paintings were carried outside the building so that those who could not get in could still follow the liturgy from without. The monastery is pressed against a cliff 300 metres above the valley floor, and it is reached only by the path that climbs the slope. And the Ottoman sultans who confirmed its privileges by decree included Selim I.

items.text: Основанный в четвёртом веке, монастырь обязан большей частью своего нынешнего облика тринадцатому веку, эпохе Трапезундской империи. Он начинался как природная пещера, превращённая в церковь, и за века разросся в пятиэтажный комплекс. Османские султаны подтверждали его привилегии указами; в ходе обмена населением 1923 года он опустел.

items.text: А вы знали? Внешняя стена скальной церкви тоже расписана фресками: росписи вынесли наружу, чтобы те, кто не мог попасть внутрь, могли следить за литургией снаружи. Монастырь прижат к утёсу на высоте 300 метров над дном долины, и добраться до него можно только по тропе, взбирающейся по склону. Османские султаны подтверждали привилегии монастыря указами — среди них был Селим I.

items.text: Step inside, and look up. You are in Hagia Sophia, in İstanbul province, a monastery and church of AD 537: the domed basilica Justinian raised in five years, and for a thousand years the largest enclosed space in the world.
items.speech: Step inside, and look up. You are in Hagia Sophia, in İstanbul province, a monastery and church of AD 537: the domed basilica Justinian raised in five years, and for a thousand years the largest enclosed space in the world.

items.text: Its story begins in fire. In 532 the Nika riots burned the earlier church, and Justinian replaced it with the present building in just five years and ten months. His architects, Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus, were specialists in geometry and mechanics, and the pendentives that carry the dome were applied here at this scale for the first time. After 1453 it became a mosque; in 1935, a museum; and in 2020, a mosque once again.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the main dome, the mosaics, the Sultan's loge, the marble doors and, if you look closely, the Viking inscription.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the main dome, the mosaics, the Sultan's loge, the marble doors and, if you look closely, the Viking inscription.

items.text: Did you know? On a marble parapet in the north gallery, a runic inscription reads 'Halfdan carved this'. It was probably scratched by one of the emperor's Varangian guards. The dome stands 55 metres high and 31 metres across, and for a thousand years it covered the largest enclosed space in the world. The ring of forty windows at its base hides its weight and makes it seem to float; Procopius wrote that it looked as if it hung from heaven on a golden chain.

items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Hagia Sophia in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 537 nach Christus Die Kuppelbasilika, die Justinian in fünf Jahren errichten ließ und die tausend Jahre lang der größte geschlossene Raum der Welt war.

items.text: Justinian ersetzte die im Nika-Aufstand von 532 niedergebrannte Kirche in fünf Jahren und zehn Monaten durch den heutigen Bau. Seine Architekten, Anthemios von Tralleis und Isidor von Milet, waren Fachleute für Geometrie und Mechanik; die Pendentiflösung, die die Kuppel trägt, wurde hier zum ersten Mal in diesem Maßstab angewandt. items.text: Юстиниан заменил церковь, сгоревшую во время восстания «Ника» в 532 году, нынешним зданием за пять лет и десять месяцев. Его архитекторы, Анфимий из Тралл и Исидор из Милета, были специалистами в геометрии и механике; решение с парусами, несущими купол, впервые было применено здесь в таком масштабе. После 1453 года она стала мечетью, в 1935 году — музеем, а в 2020 году снова мечетью.

items.text: А вы знали? На мраморном парапете северной галереи есть руническая надпись, вероятно нацарапанная одним из варяжских гвардейцев императора; она читается как «Хальвдан вырезал это». Купол возвышается на 55 метров и имеет 31 метр в поперечнике, и тысячу лет он накрывал самое большое закрытое пространство в мире. Кольцо из сорока окон у основания купола скрывает его вес и создаёт впечатление, будто он парит; Прокопий писал, что купол словно подвешен к небу на золотой цепи.

items.text: Chora Manastırı'nın kilisesi 11. yüzyılda kuruldu. items.text: Step inside Chora, or Kariye, a monastery and church in İstanbul province whose story runs through the 11th–14th century AD. This is the masterpiece of late Byzantine mosaic and fresco, holding the most complete surviving programme of Palaiologan painting. Let your eyes adjust, and look up.

items.text: The church of the Chora monastery was founded in the eleventh century. Its glory came later: the mosaics and frescoes date from 1315–1321, paid for by the statesman and scholar Theodore Metochites. Scene by scene, they tell the lives of the Virgin and of Christ. And in the side chapel waits the Anastasis, the best-known image in Byzantine painting.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Anastasis fresco and the mosaics of the life of the Virgin. Find your way into the Parekklesion, and look for the Portrait of Metochites.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the Anastasis fresco and the mosaics of the life of the Virgin. Find your way into the Parekklesion, and look for the Portrait of Metochites.

items.text: Did you know? In the mosaic above the door, the donor Theodore Metochites is shown presenting Christ with a model of the building he paid for. A donor holding his own work is rare in Byzantine art. In the side chapel, the Anastasis is the best-known image in Byzantine art: Christ hauls Adam and Eve out of their tombs by the wrists. As for Metochites, his own story took a sad turn. He later lost his fortune and ended his life as a monk in this same monastery, beneath the images he had paid for.

items.text: Mimar Sinan Selimiye'yi yaptığında seksen yaşını geçmişti. Ve burada, ömrü boyunca uğraştığı sorunu çözdü. Kubbeyi taşıyan ayakları mekânın kenarına iterek içeride bölünmemiş tek bir hacim elde etti. Sekiz fil ayağına oturan 31,25 metre çapındaki kubbe, Ayasofya'nınkinden geniştir. Külliye ise medrese, darülkurra, arasta ve muvakkithane ile birlikte tasarlandı.

items.text: Here in Edirne province stands the complex Sinan called his masterwork: the Selimiye Mosque, raised in 1569–1575. Look up at its dome. Resting on eight piers, it is wider than that of Hagia Sophia.
items.speech: Here in Edirne province stands the complex Sinan called his masterwork: the Selimiye Mosque, raised in 1569 to 1575. Look up at its dome. Resting on eight piers, it is wider than that of Hagia Sophia.

items.text: Sinan was past eighty when he built Selimiye, and here he solved the problem of his working life. He pushed the piers carrying the dome out to the edges of the space, and won a single undivided volume inside. The dome, 31.25 metres across and resting on eight piers, is wider than that of Hagia Sophia. And the mosque was never meant to stand alone: the complex was designed together with its colleges, its market row and its timekeeper's house.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the main dome and the eight elephant-foot piers. Look for the muezzin's platform and the tile panels, and end your walk in the Arasta market.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the main dome and the eight elephant-foot piers. Look for the muezzin's platform and the tile panels, and end your walk in the Arasta market.

items.text: Did you know? One marble column beneath the muezzin's platform carries an upside-down tulip. The story goes that the ground belonged to a tulip grower who resisted the endowment, and that the motif records his stubbornness. At 31.25 metres, the dome is wider than that of Hagia Sophia — the goal Sinan worked towards his whole life, and reached after eighty. By pushing the piers into the walls, he won a single volume broken by no column, so the mihrab is visible from every point in the mosque.

items.text: In der Selimiye, die er mit über achtzig Jahren baute, löste Sinan das Problem seines Berufslebens: Er rückte die Pfeiler, die die Kuppel tragen, an die Ränder des Raumes und gewann im Inneren einen einzigen, ungeteilten Raum. Die Kuppel mit 31,25 Metern Durchmesser auf acht Pfeilern ist breiter als die der Hagia Sophia. Die Anlage wurde zusammen mit ihren Medresen, der Ladenstraße und dem Haus des Zeitnehmers entworfen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Eine Marmorsäule unter der Muezzin-Empore trägt eine auf dem Kopf stehende Tulpe. Man erzählt, das Grundstück habe einem Tulpenzüchter gehört, der sich der Stiftung widersetzte, und das Motiv halte seinen Starrsinn fest. Mit 31,25 Metern ist die Kuppel breiter als die der Hagia Sophia – das Ziel, auf das Sinan sein ganzes Leben hinarbeitete und das er nach seinem achtzigsten Lebensjahr erreichte. Indem er die Pfeiler in die Wände rückte, gewann Sinan einen einzigen Raum, den keine Säule unterbricht: Der Mihrab ist von jedem Punkt der Moschee aus sichtbar.

items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Мечеть Селимие, провинция Эдирне. Период: 1569-1575. Комплекс, который Синан назвал своим шедевром; его купол, покоящийся на восьми опорах, шире купола Айя-Софии.

items.text: В Селимие, построенной, когда ему было уже за восемьдесят, Синан решил задачу всей своей творческой жизни: он отодвинул опоры, несущие купол, к краям пространства и получил внутри единый неразделённый объём. Купол диаметром 31,25 метра на восьми опорах шире купола Айя-Софии. Комплекс проектировался вместе с медресе, торговым рядом и домом хранителя времени.

items.text: А вы знали? Одна мраморная колонна под площадкой муэдзина несёт перевёрнутый тюльпан. Рассказывают, что земля принадлежала разводчику тюльпанов, который сопротивлялся передаче её в вакф, и этот мотив запечатлел его упрямство. Купол диаметром 31,25 метра шире купола Айя-Софии — это цель, к которой Синан стремился всю жизнь и которой достиг после восьмидесяти лет. Отодвинув опоры в стены, Синан получил единый объём, не прерываемый ни одной колонной: михраб виден из любой точки мечети.

items.text: Bu hikâye bir çiftle başlar. Mengücekli beyi Ahmet Şah ve eşi Turan Melek, 1228-29'da yan yana bir cami ve bir darüşşifa yaptırdı. Yapıyı benzersiz kılan ise taş kapılarıdır: Kuzey Kapısı, yani Cennet Kapısı; Batı Kapısı, yani Tekstil Kapısı; ve Darüşşifa Kapısı. items.text: You are standing before the Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, in Sivas province, built in 1228–1229. A mosque and a hospital, side by side, whose carved portals have no equal in Anatolia. It is no surprise that this was among the first sites in Türkiye inscribed by UNESCO.
items.speech: You are standing before the Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, in Sivas province, built in 1228 to 1229. A mosque and a hospital, side by side, whose carved portals have no equal in Anatolia. It is no surprise that this was among the first sites in Türkiye inscribed by UNESCO.

items.text: In 1228–29 the Mengücekid ruler Ahmet Şah and his wife Turan Melek built a mosque and a hospital side by side: a place for prayer and a place for healing. What makes the complex singular is its portals. The North (Paradise), West (Textile) and Hospital doorways carry carved ornament of a depth and volume unmatched in Islamic architecture. And inside the hospital, it is said, patients were treated with music.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Paradise Portal and the Textile Portal, then the Hospital Portal. Step inside to see the wooden minbar, and end in the hospital courtyard.

items.text: Did you know? On certain days of the year the sun casts, across the carving of the west portal, the silhouette of a figure at prayer — an effect taken to be part of the design. The carving on the portals is so deep that the stone reads as woven cloth; no other ornament in Islamic architecture works at this scale or with this freedom. And listen: the hospital is held to have treated patients with the sound of water and with music, its courtyard acoustics designed for that very purpose.

items.text: Haliç'e bakan tepedesiniz. Burada Sinan'ın 1550-1557 yılları arasında kurduğu Süleymaniye Camii ve külliyesi duruyor. Sinan burayı tek bir yapı olarak değil, bir mahalle ölçeğinde tasarladı: cami, medreseler, darüşşifa, hamam ve imaret. Hoş geldiniz.

items.text: Bu külliye, Sinan'ın olgunluk dönemi eseri. 1550-1557 arasında Kanuni Sultan Süleyman için yapıldı. Ama cami tek başına düşünülmedi: dört medrese, tıp medresesi, darüşşifa, imaret, hamam, kervansaray ve türbelerle birlikte bir kent parçası olarak tasarlandı. Bir ayrıntı daha var; gözle göremezsiniz ama kulağınızla hissedersiniz: kubbenin akustiği için duvar içlerine boşluklu küpler yerleştirildi.

items.text: Gezerken önce ana kubbenin altında durun. Sonra Kanuni ve Hürrem türbelerini ziyaret edin, medreselerin ve darüşşifanın arasında dolaşın. Ayrılmadan önce de Sinan'ın türbesine uğramayı unutmayın.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Caminin kandillerinden çıkan is boşa gitmezdi: tavandaki hava akımıyla tek bir odada toplanırdı. Biriken kurum da hattatlar için mürekkep yapımında kullanılırdı. Duvarların içine akustik için boşluklu küpler yerleştirildi; bu sayede imamın sesi mikrofonsuz olarak caminin her yerinden duyulur. Ve son bir ayrıntı: Sinan kendi türbesini külliyenin dışına, köşedeki mütevazı bir yere yaptırdı. Türbe, yaptığı camiye değil, ona giden yola bakar.

items.text: On the hill above the Golden Horn rises a complex planned at the scale of a whole neighbourhood. You are at Süleymaniye Mosque, in İstanbul province, built between 1550–1557 by Sinan: mosque, colleges, hospital, baths and kitchens, all in one design.
items.speech: On the hill above the Golden Horn rises a complex planned at the scale of a whole neighbourhood. You are at Süleymaniye Mosque, in İstanbul province, built between 1550 to 1557 by Sinan: mosque, colleges, hospital, baths and kitchens, all in one design.

items.text: This is Sinan's mature work, built for Süleyman the Magnificent between 1550 and 1557. The mosque was never meant to stand alone; it was designed as a piece of city, with four colleges, a medical school, a hospital, a soup kitchen, baths, a caravanserai and tombs. Even its walls hide a secret: hollow jars were set into them to serve the acoustics of the dome.

items.text: As you wander, look up first at the Main dome. Then don't miss the Tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem, the Colleges and the Hospital, and finally seek out Sinan's tomb.
items.speech: As you wander, look up first at the Main dome. Then don't miss the Tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem, the Colleges and the Hospital, and finally seek out Sinan's tomb.

items.text: Did you know? Soot from the mosque's lamps was drawn by the airflow into a single chamber, where it was collected and made into ink for calligraphers. The hollow jars built into the walls work for the acoustics, so that without any amplification the imam is heard everywhere in the mosque. And Sinan placed his own tomb outside the complex, in a modest corner, facing not the mosque he built but the road leading to it.

items.text: Als Werk von Sinans Reifezeit wurde die Anlage zwischen 1550 und 1557 für Süleyman den Prächtigen erbaut. In die Wände wurden hohle Krüge eingesetzt, die der Akustik der Kuppel dienen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Der Ruß der Moscheelampen wurde vom Luftstrom in eine einzige Kammer gelenkt, wo man ihn sammelte und zu Tinte für Kalligrafen verarbeitete. Für die Akustik wurden hohle Krüge in die Wände eingebaut: Ohne Verstärkung ist der Imam überall in der Moschee zu hören. Sinan legte sein eigenes Grabmal außerhalb der Anlage an, in einer bescheidenen Ecke – nicht der Moschee zugewandt, die er erbaute, sondern dem Weg dorthin.

items.text: Зрелое творение Синана, комплекс был построен для Сулеймана Великолепного между 1550 и 1557 годами. Мечеть проектировалась не сама по себе, а как часть города — с четырьмя медресе, медицинской школой, лечебницей, бесплатной кухней, банями, караван-сараем и гробницами. В стены были вмурованы полые сосуды, служащие акустике купола.

items.text: А вы знали? Копоть от светильников мечети потоком воздуха уносилась в одну-единственную камеру, где её собирали и делали из неё чернила для каллиграфов. Ради акустики в стены были встроены полые сосуды: без всякого усиления имама слышно в любой части мечети. Синан поместил собственную гробницу за пределами комплекса, в скромном углу, — обращённой не к построенной им мечети, а к дороге, ведущей к ней.

items.text: This is Topkapı Palace, in İstanbul province, dating from the 1460s. It was built not as a single building but as a compound, growing around four courtyards, and from here the Ottomans ruled for four centuries.
items.speech: This is Topkapı Palace, in İstanbul province, dating from the 1460s. It was built not as a single building but as a compound, growing around four courtyards, and from here the Ottomans ruled for four centuries.

items.text: After the conquest, Mehmed II set his palace on the point where the Marmara, the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn meet. Topkapı is not one building but a compound of kiosks, dormitories and service blocks strung along four courtyards. As you move inward, access narrows court by court, until the fourth court, open only to the sultan and his closest circle. The palace served until the court moved to Dolmabahçe in the nineteenth century.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Gate of Salutation, the Harem and the Treasury. Seek out the Sacred Relics and the Baghdad Kiosk too, and save some time for the Palace kitchens.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the Gate of Salutation, the Harem and the Treasury. Seek out the Sacred Relics and the Baghdad Kiosk too, and save some time for the Palace kitchens.

items.text: Did you know? The palace kitchens fed close to five thousand people a day; their chimneys were redesigned by Sinan, and today the buildings hold the collection of Chinese porcelain. The palace is a compound rather than a building: four courtyards deep, each admitting fewer people than the last, until the fourth, reserved for the sultan and his closest circle. And look closely at the İznik tiles of the Harem: they carry the coral red that was lost in the sixteenth century and never reproduced.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Topkapı-Palast in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 1460er-Jahre. Ein Palast, der nicht als einzelnes Gebäude, sondern als Anlage um vier Höfe herum wuchs und von dem aus die Osmanen vier Jahrhunderte lang regierten.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Topkapı-Palast in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 1460er-Jahre. Ein Palast, der nicht als einzelnes Gebäude, sondern als Anlage um vier Höfe herum wuchs und von dem aus die Osmanen vier Jahrhunderte lang regierten.

items.text: Nach der Eroberung errichtete Mehmed II. seinen Palast auf der Landspitze, an der Marmarameer, Bosporus und Goldenes Horn zusammentreffen. Topkapı ist kein einzelnes Gebäude, sondern eine Anlage aus Pavillons, Schlafsälen und Wirtschaftsbauten, aufgereiht an vier Höfen; der Zugang wird nach innen immer enger bis zum vierten Hof, der nur dem Sultan und seinem engsten Kreis offenstand. Er diente als Residenz, bis der Hof im neunzehnten Jahrhundert nach Dolmabahçe umzog.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Tor der Begrüßung, Harem, Schatzkammer, Heilige Reliquien, Bagdad-Pavillon und Palastküchen.
items.speech: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Tor der Begrüßung, Harem, Schatzkammer, Heilige Reliquien, Bagdad-Pavillon und Palastküchen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Palastküchen versorgten täglich fast fünftausend Menschen; ihre Schornsteine wurden von Sinan umgestaltet, und heute beherbergen die Gebäude die Sammlung chinesischen Porzellans. Der Palast ist eine Anlage, kein Gebäude: vier Höfe tief, von denen jeder weniger Menschen einlässt, bis der vierte allein dem Sultan offensteht. Die İznik-Fliesen des Harems tragen das Korallenrot, das im sechzehnten Jahrhundert verloren ging und nie wieder hergestellt wurde.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Дворец Топкапы, провинция Стамбул. Период: 1460-е годы. Дворец, построенный не как единое здание, а как комплекс, разраставшийся вокруг четырёх дворов; отсюда османы правили четыре столетия.
items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Дворец Топкапы, провинция Стамбул. Период: 1460-е годы. Дворец, построенный не как единое здание, а как комплекс, разраставшийся вокруг четырёх дворов; отсюда османы правили четыре столетия.

items.text: После завоевания Мехмед II поставил свой дворец на мысу, где сходятся Мраморное море, Босфор и Золотой Рог. Топкапы — это не одно здание, а комплекс павильонов, спален и служебных корпусов, нанизанных вдоль четырёх дворов; доступ сужается по мере продвижения вглубь вплоть до четвёртого двора, открытого лишь для султана и его ближайшего окружения. Дворец служил резиденцией, пока в девятнадцатом веке двор не переехал в Долмабахче.

items.text: А вы знали? Дворцовые кухни кормили почти пять тысяч человек в день; их дымоходы перестроил Синан, а сегодня в этих зданиях хранится коллекция китайского фарфора. Дворец — это комплекс, а не здание: четыре двора в глубину, каждый из которых пропускает всё меньше людей, пока четвёртый не оказывается открыт лишь для султана. Изникские изразцы гарема несут коралловый красный цвет, секрет которого был утрачен в шестнадцатом веке и так и не был воспроизведён.

items.text: On a slope above the Silk Road at Doğubayazıt, in Ağrı province, stands İshak Pasha Palace, built in 1685–1784. In a single building it fuses Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian architecture. Let us discover how.
items.speech: On a slope above the Silk Road at Doğubayazıt, in Ağrı province, stands İshak Pasha Palace, built in 1685 to 1784. In a single building it fuses Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian architecture. Let us discover how.

items.text: Work began in 1685 on the rock above the Doğubayazıt pass of the Silk Road, and it took about a century to finish. Inside a single walled island of building, the palace gathers a mosque, a tomb, a harem, public quarters, a council hall, a prison and baths. Look closely at the stonework: Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian traditions are carried together. And the palace is held to have had a central heating system.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the grand portal, then the harem, the mosque and the tomb, and finally the council hall.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the grand portal, then the harem, the mosque and the tomb, and finally the council hall.

items.text: Did you know? The palace's gilded door leaves were removed to Russia in 1917, and today they are displayed in a museum in Moscow. The palace is also held to have had central heating and a drainage system, and no other residence in eighteenth-century Anatolia is known to have had either. On the same façade, Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian stonework stand side by side, a rare case in which no one style takes over.

Üç büyük kulenin her biri bir vezirin sorumluluğuna verildi ve kuleler bugün hâlâ onların adıyla anılıyor. Kaleye yerleştirilen toplar ise Boğaz'dan geçen gemileri durdurabiliyordu. Artık bu sulardan izinsiz geçmek mümkün değildi.

items.text: Before you stands Rumeli Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province, built in 1452. It went up in just four months at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, before the siege of Constantinople, with one purpose: to cut the city off from relief by sea.
items.speech: Before you stands Rumeli Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province, built in 1452. It went up in just four months at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, before the siege of Constantinople, with one purpose: to cut the city off from relief by sea.

items.text: Before the siege of Constantinople, Mehmed II built this fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, directly opposite Anadolu Hisarı. Construction took four months, in the summer of 1452. Each of the three great towers was assigned to a vizier, and each still carries his name. And the guns mounted here could stop any ship in the strait.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the great towers: Halil Pasha Tower, Saruca Pasha Tower and Zağanos Pasha Tower. Follow the curtain walls between them, and finish at the Amphitheatre.

items.text: Did you know? While the fortress was being built, a Venetian ship that tried to run the strait was sunk — an act that effectively ended Byzantine hopes of relief before the siege had even begun. The fortress went up in four months before the siege of Constantinople, and each of its three great towers was assigned to a vizier, whose name it still carries.

Üzerlerindeki kitabeler ve hayvan kabartmaları, kenti yöneten her hanedanın kendi imzasını bıraktığı bir taş arşivi oluşturuyor.

items.text: Look at the dark stone rising before you. This is Diyarbakır Fortress, with the Hevsel Gardens at its feet, in Diyarbakır province. Its walls date from the 4th century AD: 5.8 kilometres of basalt, reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit after the Great Wall, wrapping around the Hevsel Gardens on the Tigris.
items.speech: Look at the dark stone rising before you. This is Diyarbakır Fortress, with the Hevsel Gardens at its feet, in Diyarbakır province. Its walls date from the 4th century AD: 5.8 kilometres of basalt, reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit after the Great Wall, wrapping around the Hevsel Gardens on the Tigris.

items.text: The walls took their present form under Rome in the fourth century AD. After that, one power after another repaired and extended them: Byzantines, Marwanids, Artuqids, Aq Qoyunlu and Ottomans. Built of black basalt, the circuit runs 5.8 kilometres, with 82 towers and four main gates. Now look closely at the towers. Their inscriptions and animal reliefs form a stone archive, in which every dynasty that held the city left its signature.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Ulu Beden Tower and the Seven Brothers Tower, then pass the Mardin Gate and the Urfa Gate. Look out over the Hevsel Gardens, and end at the Inner citadel.

items.text: Did you know? The Hevsel Gardens below the walls have been farmed without a break for eight thousand years. They fed the city, and UNESCO inscribed them together with the walls as a single whole. The 5.8 kilometres of basalt are reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit in the world after the Great Wall. And the inscriptions on the towers carry the signature of every dynasty that held the city, from Rome to the Ottomans. This wall is an archive of power, written in stone.

items.text: Safranbolu bir yol kasabasıydı. İstanbul'u Karadeniz'e ve Anadolu'ya bağlayan kervan yolu üzerinde, yolcuların konakladığı, tüccarların alışveriş yaptığı bir durak. Zenginliğini, adını da aldığı safran ticaretine ve debbağlığa borçluydu. Kent iki yerleşimden oluşur: çarşının bulunduğu Şehir ve yazlık bağ evlerinin yer aldığı Bağlar. items.text: Step into Safranbolu, a historic town in Karabük province, where the 17th–19th century still lingers in every street. Around a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand here, preserving almost intact the fabric of a trading centre on the caravan road.
items.speech: Step into Safranbolu, a historic town in Karabük province, where the 17th–19th century still lingers in every street. Around a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand here, preserving almost intact the fabric of a trading centre on the caravan road.

items.text: Safranbolu was a staging and trading town on the caravan road linking Istanbul to the Black Sea and inland Anatolia. Its wealth came from tanning, and from the saffron trade that gave it its name. In truth, the town is two settlements: Şehir, gathered around the market, and Bağlar, with its summer vineyard houses. And then a stroke of luck: railways and highways passed it by, which is exactly why its fabric survived.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Cinci Han, the Köprülü Mehmet Pasha Mosque and the Shoemakers' arasta, then make your way to the Kaymakamlar House and the historic bazaar.

items.text: Did you know? Most of the houses still have their revolving cupboard between the family quarters and the guest rooms, through which food could be passed without either side seeing the other. Around a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand. The railway and the highway both passed the town by, and that is what preserved it. And the town is named for the saffron grown around it, a spice once weighed against gold.

items.text: Step into Cumalıkızık, a historic town in Bursa province whose story begins in the 14th century. This is a foundation village from the Ottomans' first century, lived in on the same plan for seven hundred years. Its cobbled lanes and overhanging houses are still intact.
items.speech: Step into Cumalıkızık, a historic town in Bursa province whose story begins in the 14th century. This is a foundation village from the Ottomans' first century, lived in on the same plan for seven hundred years. Its cobbled lanes and overhanging houses are still intact.

items.text: In the Ottomans' first century, Cumalıkızık was one of the endowment villages that fed Bursa. Because its income was tied to a foundation, it was never broken up — and that is the secret of what you see. Of its roughly 270 houses, more than half still stand. Look up: their three storeys of timber-laced mudbrick almost meet overhead across the lanes. The street pattern and plot divisions have not changed since the fourteenth century.

items.text: Did you know? The village was inscribed by UNESCO not on its own but together with Bursa's monuments, under the title 'Bursa and Cumalıkızık: the Birth of the Ottoman Empire'. Because its income was tied to a foundation, it was never broken up, so its street pattern and plot divisions are unchanged since the fourteenth century. More than half of its roughly 270 houses still stand, and people still live in them: this is a working village, not a museum.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Kasımiye Medresesi'nin avlusundaki uzun havuz bir hikâye anlatır. Su kaynağından çıkar, havuzda durulur, sonra akıp gider; tıpkı bir insan ömrü gibi. items.text: Step into Old Mardin, a historic town in Mardin province whose fabric belongs to the 12th–19th century. The town is terraced down the slope above the Mesopotamian plain, and here carved limestone madrasas, mosques and Syriac churches stand side by side. Take a breath and enjoy the view.

items.text: Mardin is terraced down the south face of a limestone ridge that commands the Mesopotamian plain. Each house's roof serves as the courtyard of the one above. The result? The whole town enjoys an unbroken view and natural ventilation. The fabric of the town was shaped under the Artuqids, and here mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street. Look closely at the walls: carved stone is the region's distinctive art.

items.text: Did you know? The long pool in the courtyard of the Kasımiye Madrasa was designed to describe a human life: water rises from its source, rests in the basin, and flows away. The town is terraced so that each house's roof is the courtyard of the one above, giving every house an unbroken view over the plain. Mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street, and the Syriac monastery of Deyrulzafaran has been in the same place for 1,500 years.

items.text: I. Ahmed bu camiyi yaptırmaya karar verdiğinde henüz on dokuz yaşındaydı. Yer olarak Ayasofya'nın karşısını, Bizans Büyük Sarayı'nın kalıntılarını seçti. Ve bir ilke imza attı: savaş ganimeti olmadan cami yaptıran ilk padişah oldu. Yapıyı 1609-1617 arasında Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa tamamladı. Ama altı minare kararı beklenmedik bir tartışma doğurdu; bu, Mekke'deki Harem-i Şerif'le eşitlik iddiası sayıldı. Çözüm mü? Mekke'ye yedinci bir minare eklendi.

Sipariş o kadar büyüktü ki atölyelerin fiyatları yükseldi ve İznik çiniciliği bu işten sonra bir daha toparlanamadı. Altı minare ise o sırada yalnızca Mekke'deki Harem-i Şerif'te vardı; iddia tartışma yaratınca Mekke'ye bir minare daha eklendi. Cami bugün de ibadete açık; ziyaret saatleri namaz vakitlerine göre değişir ve giriş ücretsizdir. Ve son olarak: yapı Bizans Büyük Sarayı'nın üzerine kuruldu. Sarayın mozaik tabanı bugün caminin arkasındaki müzede, yerinde duruyor.

items.text: Before you rises the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province, built in 1609–1617. Count its six minarets, then step inside to meet the twenty thousand İznik tiles that line its walls. It was raised directly opposite Hagia Sophia, over the old Byzantine palace.
items.speech: Before you rises the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province, built in 1609 to 1617. Count its six minarets, then step inside to meet the twenty thousand İznik tiles that line its walls. It was raised directly opposite Hagia Sophia, over the old Byzantine palace.

items.text: Ahmed I was just nineteen when he chose his site: the ruins of the Byzantine Great Palace, facing Hagia Sophia. He became the first sultan to raise such a mosque without the spoils of a victory to pay for it. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa completed the work between 1609 and 1617. And those six minarets? They were read as a claim to equal the sanctuary at Mecca, so a seventh was added there.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the main dome and its semi-domes, the six minarets and the İznik tiles. Look out for the Imperial Lodge, visit the Tomb of Ahmed I, and finish in the courtyard with its fountain.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the main dome and its semi-domes, the six minarets and the İznik tiles. Look out for the Imperial Lodge, visit the Tomb of Ahmed I, and finish in the courtyard with its fountain.

items.text: Did you know? The tiles that give it the name 'Blue Mosque' came from İznik, and the order was so large that it drove the workshops' prices past recovery — İznik tilemaking never regained its footing. At the time, six minarets were matched only by the sanctuary at Mecca; when the claim caused offence, a further minaret was added there. The mosque is still a place of prayer, so visiting hours shift with the prayer times, and there is no entry charge. And beneath it lies the Byzantine Great Palace, whose mosaic floor still rests in place in the museum behind the mosque.

items.text: Ahmed I. war neunzehn, als er beschloss, seine Moschee auf den Ruinen des byzantinischen Großen Palastes gegenüber der Hagia Sophia zu bauen, und er wurde der erste Sultan, der eine Moschee errichtete, ohne sie mit der Beute eines Sieges zu bezahlen. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa vollendete sie zwischen 1609 und 1617. Als ihre sechs Minarette als Anspruch gedeutet wurden, dem Heiligtum in Mekka gleichzukommen, wurde dort ein siebtes hinzugefügt.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Fliesen, die sie zur „Blauen Moschee“ machen, kamen aus İznik, und der Auftrag war so groß, dass er die Preise der Werkstätten unwiederbringlich in die Höhe trieb – die Fliesenkunst von İznik kam nie wieder auf die Beine. Sechs Minarette besaß damals nur das Heiligtum in Mekka; als der Anspruch Anstoß erregte, wurde dort ein weiteres Minarett hinzugefügt. Die Moschee wird noch immer zum Gebet genutzt, daher richten sich die Besuchszeiten nach den Gebetszeiten. Der Eintritt ist frei. Sie wurde über dem byzantinischen Großen Palast erbaut, dessen Mosaikboden noch heute an Ort und Stelle im Museum hinter ihr liegt.

items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Голубая мечеть (мечеть Султанахмет), провинция Стамбул. Период: 1609-1617. Известная своими шестью минаретами и двадцатью тысячами изникских изразцов на стенах, мечеть была возведена прямо напротив Айя-Софии, на месте старого византийского дворца.

items.text: Ахмеду I было девятнадцать лет, когда он решил построить свою мечеть на руинах Большого императорского дворца византийцев напротив Айя-Софии, и он стал первым султаном, возведшим мечеть без военной добычи, которая оплатила бы строительство. Седефкяр Мехмед-ага завершил её между 1609 и 1617 годами. Когда её шесть минаретов восприняли как притязание на равенство со святилищем в Мекке, там был добавлен седьмой.

items.text: А вы знали? Изразцы, сделавшие её «Голубой мечетью», привезли из Изника, и заказ был так велик, что безвозвратно взвинтил цены мастерских, — изникское изразцовое производство так и не оправилось. Шесть минаретов в то время были только у святилища в Мекке; когда это притязание вызвало недовольство, там добавили ещё один минарет. Мечеть по-прежнему используется для молитвы, поэтому часы посещения меняются в зависимости от времени намаза. Вход бесплатный. Она построена над Большим императорским дворцом византийцев, мозаичный пол которого до сих пор лежит на своём месте в музее позади мечети.

items.text: You are about to enter the Great Mosque of Bursa, a mosque and complex in Bursa province, built in 1396–1400. It is the masterpiece of the multi-domed plan: twenty domes carried on twelve piers. And at its centre stands a fountain, lit through an opening left where a dome would be.
items.speech: You are about to enter the Great Mosque of Bursa, a mosque and complex in Bursa province, built in 1396 to 1400. It is the masterpiece of the multi-domed plan: twenty domes carried on twelve piers. And at its centre stands a fountain, lit through an opening left where a dome would be.

items.text: Behind this building lies a promise. Bayezid I had vowed twenty mosques if he won at Nicopolis; on his return, he built one mosque with twenty domes instead. It was finished in 1400. Two years later, when Timur took Bursa, it was damaged, and afterwards it was repaired. Its fountain stands beneath the opening left where one of the domes would have been.

items.text: Did you know? More than 190 calligraphic panels cover its walls, most of them by nineteenth-century masters, so the mosque can be read as a museum of the art. And the fountain at the centre sits under the opening left where a dome would be: with no courtyard, the interior does the courtyard's work.

items.text: Mehmed I was the sultan who brought the Ottomans out of the interregnum. He died in 1421 and was buried on the slope of the complex he had built for himself in Bursa. items.text: Did you know? The tiles over the cenotaph were made in the coloured-glaze technique their masters brought from Tabriz, and the masters' signatures can still be read. The turquoise tiling that gives the tomb its name was renewed after the earthquake of 1855, though some of the original tiles survive inside. And the cenotaph of Mehmed I is the most elaborate piece of Ottoman tilework surviving from the Bursa period.

items.text: Step quietly into Eşrefoğlu Mosque, a mosque and complex in Konya province, built in 1297–1299. Look around you: forty-two cedar columns carry a wooden ceiling that is still in place after seven centuries. At the centre, the snow well is left open, so that winter snow can keep the timber from drying out.
items.speech: Step quietly into Eşrefoğlu Mosque, a mosque and complex in Konya province, built in 1297 to 1299. Look around you: forty-two cedar columns carry a wooden ceiling that is still in place after seven centuries. At the centre, the snow well is left open, so that winter snow can keep the timber from drying out.

items.text: The mosque was built between 1297 and 1299 for Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey. It is the largest and best preserved of Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques: for seven centuries, forty-two cedar columns have carried its flat timber ceiling. In 2023 it became one of those inscribed as the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia.
items.speech: The mosque was built between 1297 and 1299 for Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey. It is the largest and best preserved of Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques: for seven centuries, forty-two cedar columns have carried its flat timber ceiling. In 2023 it became one of those inscribed as the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the cedar columns, the snow well, the tiled mihrab, the wooden minbar and, as you come or go, the portal.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the cedar columns, the snow well, the tiled mihrab, the wooden minbar and, as you come or go, the portal.

items.text: Did you know? The snow well at the centre is engineering, not ornament. In winter, snow falling through the roof melts and evaporates, keeping the air damp enough that the timber does not split. None of the forty-two cedar columns has ever been replaced: the same trees have carried the roof for seven centuries. And in 2023 Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques entered the World Heritage List — with Eşrefoğlu the largest of them all.

items.text: You are now at the Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, a mosque and complex in Diyarbakır province, rebuilt in 1091. It is one of Anatolia's oldest mosques. Look at its two-storey courtyard front: its columns and capitals were lifted straight out of the city's Roman buildings.
items.speech: You are now at the Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, a mosque and complex in Diyarbakır province, rebuilt in 1091. It is one of Anatolia's oldest mosques. Look at its two-storey courtyard front: its columns and capitals were lifted straight out of the city's Roman buildings.

items.text: This ground has been sacred for a long time. A Roman temple stood here, and then the church of Mar Toma; when the city was taken in 639, part of the church became a mosque. The building's present form comes from the rebuilding ordered in 1091 by the Seljuk sultan Melikşah. Its two-storey courtyard front was assembled from columns and capitals lifted out of the city's Roman buildings.

Bir yangından sonra, 13. yüzyılın sonunda genişletildi ve dört bin metrekareyi aştı. Planına dikkat edin: yazlık bir avlu ve kışlık kapalı bir bölüm. Bu çift plan, Selçuklu kervansaraylarının tipik düzenidir.

items.text: Gezerken önce taç kapının önünde durun. Ardından avluya girin ve ortadaki köşk mescide bakın. Sonra kapalı kışlık hole geçin; ahırları ve depoları da görmeden ayrılmayın.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Selçuklu hanlarında konaklama, yemek ve hayvanların nallanması üç gün boyunca parasızdı; masrafı hanın vakfı karşılardı. Avlunun ortasındaki köşk mescit dört ayak üzerinde yükselir; altından geçen kervan, yükünü boşaltmadan avluya girebilirdi. Han da ikiye ayrılır: yazlık avlu ve kışlık kapalı hol. Selçuklu han planını böyle belirleyen, Anadolu'nun sert kışıydı.

items.text: Imagine the end of a long day on the road, and gates opening to welcome you. This is Sultan Han Caravanserai, in Aksaray province, built in 1229: the largest Seljuk caravanserai in Anatolia. items.text: Sultan Han was built in 1229 for Alâeddin Keykubad I, and it was the largest stop for caravans on the Konya–Aksaray–Kayseri road. After a fire it was enlarged at the end of the thirteenth century to more than four thousand square metres. Notice its two halves: an open summer court paired with a covered winter hall. That pairing is the standard Seljuk plan.

items.text: Did you know? In a Seljuk han, lodging, food and the shoeing of animals were free for three days, paid for by the endowment that ran the building. The kiosk mosque in the middle of the court stands on four piers, so a loaded caravan could pass right beneath it into the yard. And the han is split between an open summer court and a covered winter hall — the Anatolian winter, in a sense, wrote the Seljuk plan.

items.text: Here is Cendere Bridge, in Adıyaman province, built in the late 2nd century AD. This Roman bridge crosses the Cendere in a single arch. Of the four columns raised by the XVI Legion for Septimius Severus and his family, three still stand.

items.text: The bridge was built at the end of the second century AD by the XVI Legion, together with the surrounding Commagenian cities, for the emperor Septimius Severus, his wife Julia Domna and their sons. Three of the four columns still stand. And the fourth? It belonged to Geta, and it was taken down after he was murdered and his name struck from the record.

items.text: Did you know? The bridge has stood for eighteen centuries and carried vehicles until recently; traffic stopped only when a new bridge was built beside it. One of its four columns is missing: when Geta's name was struck from the record after his death, his column came down with it. And because the bridge sits on the road up to Mount Nemrut, most Commagene itineraries cross it.

items.text: The bridge was built over the Batman river in 1147 under the Artuqids, and its single arch spans more than thirty-eight metres. Why so wide? The width was a defence against the spring floods that carry snowmelt down the valley. Chambers in its flanks were set aside so that travellers and caravans could spend the night.

items.text: Did you know? The span is wider than the dome of Hagia Sophia, and very few medieval stone arches were ever built at that scale. And the rooms in the bridge's flanks were built so that travellers could spend a winter night inside the bridge itself.

items.text: Bu kümbet 1276 dolaylarında Şah Cihan Hatun için yapıldı ve bugün Kayseri'nin Selçuklu mezar anıtlarının en tanınmışı. Peki neden 'döner'? Çevresinde yürümeye başlayın, anlayacaksınız: on iki yüzlü gövde ve konik külah, yürüyen birine yapı dönüyormuş izlenimi verir. Bir ayrıntı daha: altındaki cenazelik odası, gövdenin içindeki mescitten ayrıdır.

items.text: Gezerken önce konik külaha bakın, sonra gövdedeki hayat ağacı kabartmasını, çift başlı kartalı ve aslan figürlerini tek tek bulun. Altta, cenazeliği de mutlaka görün.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Gövdedeki çift başlı kartal Selçuklu hanedan armasıydı; yüzyıllar sonra Avrupa hanedanlarının armalarında da yer alacaktı. Bir itiraf da yapalım: kümbet aslında dönmez. Adı, on iki yüzlü gövdenin çevresinde yürüyen birine yapı dönüyormuş gibi görünmesinden gelir. Ve hayat ağacı kabartmasına bir daha bakın: iki yanında karşılıklı duran hayvan figürleri, Orta Asya'dan gelen bir bezeme geleneğini sürdürür.

items.text: Before you stands Döner Kümbet, a tomb in Kayseri province, built c. 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun. Walk slowly around its twelve sides. Its conical cap and its bands of tree-of-life, double-headed eagle and lion reliefs have made it the emblem of Seljuk funerary architecture.

items.text: Built around 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun, this is the best known of Kayseri's Seljuk tomb towers. Its twelve-sided body and conical cap give it its name: as you walk around it, the building seems to turn. Beneath your feet, the burial chamber is kept separate from the prayer room inside the shaft.

items.text: As you wander around the tomb, don't miss the conical cap, the tree of life relief, the double-headed eagle and the lion figures, and finally the crypt below.
items.speech: As you wander around the tomb, don't miss the conical cap, the tree of life relief, the double-headed eagle and the lion figures, and finally the crypt below.

items.text: Did you know? The double-headed eagle on its shaft was a Seljuk dynastic emblem, a device that would turn up centuries later on European coats of arms. And no, the tomb does not really turn: the name comes from the way the twelve-sided shaft seems to rotate as you walk around it. The animals facing each other across the tree-of-life relief continue a decorative tradition carried all the way from Central Asia.

items.text: Başınızı kaldırın: İstanbul'da, iki tepenin arasını iki katlı kemerlerle bağlayan Bozdoğan Kemeri'nin önündesiniz. MS 373'ten kalan bu su kemeri, kenti Trakya'daki kaynaklara bağlayan 250 kilometrelik hattın son halkasıydı. Osmanlı döneminde de onarıldı ve kullanılmaya devam etti. Bozdoğan Kemeri sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz.

items.text: Look up at two tiers of arches striding across the valley between two hills. This is the Valens Aqueduct, in İstanbul province, dating from AD 373. It was the last link in a 250-kilometre line from the Thracian springs, and it was kept in repair and in use through the Ottoman centuries.
items.speech: Look up at two tiers of arches striding across the valley between two hills. This is the Valens Aqueduct, in İstanbul province, dating from AD 373. items.text: The aqueduct was completed in AD 373 under the emperor Valens. It formed the last link inside the city of a long line that ran all the way from the springs of Thrace, carrying water over the valley between two hills to the cisterns. In Ottoman centuries it was repaired again and again, and so the city's water system kept working for hundreds of years.

items.text: Did you know? The surviving stretch is about 900 metres long, and today one of the city's busiest roads runs beneath its arches. Yet the aqueduct was only the last link of a water line hundreds of kilometres long, reaching back to the springs of Thrace. It was maintained under the Ottomans too, so the city's water ran along this Roman line for centuries.

items.text: Şimdi yerin altındasınız: Yerebatan Sarnıcı. İstanbul'da, MS 6. yüzyıldan kalma bir sarnıç. Çevrenizde 336 sütun bu yeraltı su deposunu taşıyor. Kuşatma günlerinde sarayın ve çevresinin suyu burada tutulurdu. Ve iki sütunun altında sizi beklenmedik yüzler bekliyor: devşirme Medusa başları, ters ve yan yatırılmış hâlde.

items.text: Hikâye bir isyanla başlar. Justinianus, 532'deki Nika ayaklanmasından sonra bu sarnıcı yaptırdı. 138 metreye 65 metrelik bir alanı kaplayan sarnıç, seksen bin metreküpe yakın su tutardı. Su Bozdoğan Kemeri'nden gelir, buradan Büyük Saray'a ve çevresine dağıtılırdı. Sonra tuhaf bir şey oldu: Osmanlı döneminde sarnıcın varlığı unutuldu. Onu 16. yüzyılda yeniden kayda geçiren, evlerinin bodrumundan kova sarkıtıp balık çıkaran mahallelilerdi.

items.text: Step down into the Basilica Cistern, a cistern in İstanbul province from the 6th century AD. Imagine a forest of 336 columns, hidden underground. This reservoir held the water of the palace quarter through a siege. And look out for two of its columns in particular: they stand on reused Medusa heads, one upside down and one on its side.
items.speech: Step down into the Basilica Cistern, a cistern in İstanbul province from the 6th century AD. Imagine a forest of 336 columns, hidden underground. This reservoir held the water of the palace quarter through a siege. And look out for two of its columns in particular: they stand on reused Medusa heads, one upside down and one on its side.

items.text: After the Nika revolt of 532, Justinian had this cistern built. It covers 138 by 65 metres and held close to eighty thousand cubic metres of water, fed from the Valens aqueduct and sent on to the Great Palace quarter. Then, under the Ottomans, it was forgotten. So how was it found again? In the sixteenth century it was recorded once more — only because householders were lowering buckets through their cellar floors and pulling up fish.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the 336 columns, the Medusa heads, the Column of Tears and the brick vaults above them.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the 336 columns, the Medusa heads, the Column of Tears and the brick vaults above them.

items.text: Did you know? Two Medusa heads serve as column bases here, one upside down and one on its side. Why were they set that way? Nobody knows; the likeliest answer is simply that they were the right height. That fits the rest of the story: the 336 columns were gathered from different buildings, so where the heights did not match, bases were raised and capitals turned over. And one last curiosity: forgotten under the Ottomans, the cistern was recorded again in the sixteenth century only because people were pulling fish up through their cellar floors.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Yerebatan-Zisterne in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 6. Jahrhundert n. Chr. Ein unterirdischer Speicher auf 336 Säulen, der das Wasser des Palastviertels während einer Belagerung vorhielt; zwei der Säulen stehen auf wiederverwendeten Medusenhäuptern, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Yerebatan-Zisterne in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 6. Jahrhundert nach Christus Ein unterirdischer Speicher auf 336 Säulen, der das Wasser des Palastviertels während einer Belagerung vorhielt; zwei der Säulen stehen auf wiederverwendeten Medusenhäuptern, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend.

items.text: Von Justinian nach dem Nika-Aufstand von 532 erbaut, misst die Zisterne 138 mal 65 Meter und fasste fast achtzigtausend Kubikmeter Wasser, das über das Valens-Aquädukt zufloss und im Viertel des Großen Palastes verteilt wurde. Unter den Osmanen geriet sie in Vergessenheit und wurde im sechzehnten Jahrhundert nur deshalb wieder verzeichnet, weil Hausbewohner Eimer durch ihre Kellerböden hinabließen und Fische heraufzogen.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: 336 Säulen, Medusenhäupter, Tränensäule und Ziegelgewölbe.
items.speech: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: 336 Säulen, Medusenhäupter, Tränensäule und Ziegelgewölbe.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Zwei Medusenhäupter dienen als Säulenbasen, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend. Warum sie so gesetzt wurden, ist unbekannt; die wahrscheinlichste Antwort ist, dass sie einfach die richtige Höhe hatten. Ihre 336 Säulen wurden aus verschiedenen Bauten zusammengetragen; wo die Höhen nicht passten, wurden deshalb Basen erhöht und Kapitelle umgedreht. Die Zisterne war unter den Osmanen in Vergessenheit geraten und wurde im sechzehnten Jahrhundert nur deshalb wieder verzeichnet, weil Menschen Fische durch ihre Kellerböden heraufzogen.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Цистерна Йеребатан, провинция Стамбул. Период: VI век н. э. Подземное водохранилище на 336 колоннах, хранившее воду для дворцового квартала во время осады; две из колонн стоят на повторно использованных головах Медузы — одна перевёрнута, другая лежит на боку.

Период: VI век нашей эры Подземное водохранилище на 336 колоннах, хранившее воду для дворцового квартала во время осады; две из колонн стоят на повторно использованных головах Медузы, одна перевёрнута, другая лежит на боку.

items.text: Построенная Юстинианом после восстания «Ника» 532 года, цистерна занимает площадь 138 на 65 метров и вмещала почти восемьдесят тысяч кубометров воды, поступавшей по акведуку Валента и распределявшейся по кварталу Большого дворца. При османах о ней забыли, и в шестнадцатом веке её снова описали лишь потому, что жители опускали вёдра сквозь полы своих подвалов и вытаскивали рыбу.

items.text: А вы знали? Две головы Медузы служат основаниями колонн: одна перевёрнута, другая лежит на боку. Почему их установили именно так, неизвестно; вероятнее всего, они просто подходили по высоте. Её 336 колонн были собраны из разных зданий, поэтому там, где высота не совпадала, основания приподнимали, а капители переворачивали. При османах о цистерне забыли, и в шестнадцатом веке её снова описали лишь потому, что люди вытаскивали рыбу сквозь полы своих подвалов.

items.text: Boğaz kıyısındasınız, Dolmabahçe Sarayı'nda. 1843-1856 yılları arasında yapılan bu saray, Osmanlı sarayının Topkapı'dan taşındığı yer. Kıyı boyunca 600 metre uzanıyor. Muayede Salonu'nun 4,5 tonluk avizesi ve 285 odası, imparatorluğun son yüzyılının ölçeğini gözler önüne seriyor. Hoş geldiniz.

items.text: Sultan Abdülmecid, Topkapı'yı devrin diplomasisi için yetersiz buldu ve sarayı Boğaz kıyısındaki doldurulmuş koya taşıdı. Yapıyı 1843-1856 arasında Balyan ailesi inşa etti: 285 oda, 46 salon ve 600 metrelik bir rıhtım cephesi. Cumhuriyet döneminde saray, Atatürk'ün İstanbul'daki çalışma ve ikamet yeri oldu. Ve 10 Kasım 1938'de Atatürk burada öldü.

items.text: You are at Dolmabahçe Palace in İstanbul province, built in 1843–1856 — where the Ottoman court moved after Topkapı. Take in the numbers: 600 metres of façade along the Bosphorus, 285 rooms, and a 4.5-tonne chandelier in the ceremonial hall. This is the scale of the empire's last century.

items.text: Sultan Abdülmecid found Topkapı inadequate for the diplomacy of the age, so he moved the court to a filled-in bay on the Bosphorus. The Balyan family built the palace between 1843 and 1856: 285 rooms, 46 halls and six hundred metres of quay frontage. In the Republic it became Atatürk's residence and workplace in İstanbul. And it was here that he died, on 10 November 1938.

items.text: Als Sultan Abdülmecid den Topkapı-Palast für die Diplomatie seiner Zeit unzureichend fand, verlegte er den Hof an eine aufgeschüttete Bucht am Bosporus. Von der Familie Balyan zwischen 1843 und 1856 erbaut, umfasst der Palast 285 Zimmer, 46 Säle und sechshundert Meter Kaifront. In der Republik wurde er Atatürks Residenz und Arbeitsstätte in Istanbul, und er starb hier am 10. November 1938.

items.text: Когда султан Абдул-Меджид счёл Топкапы неподходящим для дипломатии своего времени, он перенёс двор в засыпанную бухту на Босфоре. Построенный семьёй Бальян между 1843 и 1856 годами, дворец насчитывает 285 комнат, 46 залов и шестьсот метров фасада вдоль набережной. При Республике он стал резиденцией и рабочим местом Ататюрка в Стамбуле, и здесь он умер 10 ноября 1938 года.

items.text: Look up at Galata Tower, a monument in İstanbul province dating from 1348. The Genoese raised it at the highest point of their Galata walls. For centuries it served as a fire watchtower, and today it is known for the view down over the Golden Horn.
items.speech: Look up at Galata Tower, a monument in İstanbul province dating from 1348. The Genoese raised it at the highest point of their Galata walls. For centuries it served as a fire watchtower, and today it is known for the view down over the Golden Horn.

items.text: The Genoese were granted their colony at Galata by Byzantium, and in 1348 they crowned its walls with this tower, calling it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it took on many roles: prison, observatory and fire watchtower. Fires and earthquakes changed its cap several times; the cone you see today dates from a twentieth-century restoration.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the conical cap and the viewing gallery. Look for the remains of the Genoese walls, and for the stone shaft of the tower itself.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the conical cap and the viewing gallery. Look for the remains of the Genoese walls, and for the stone shaft of the tower itself.

items.text: Did you know? The tower's best known story is also its least verifiable: Evliya Çelebi tells how Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi strapped on wings and glided from this tower to Üsküdar. The Genoese raised the tower in 1348 at the highest point of their own walls and named it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it was a fire watchtower, and in a city of timber, the alarm was raised from here.

items.text: Die Genuesen, denen Byzanz ihre Kolonie in Galata zugestanden hatte, krönten deren Mauern 1348 mit diesem Turm und nannten ihn Christusturm. Sein Dach wurde nach Bränden und Erdbeben mehrmals erneuert; der heutige Kegel stammt von einer Restaurierung im zwanzigsten Jahrhundert.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Evliya Çelebis Bericht, wonach Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi sich Flügel umschnallte und von diesem Turm bis nach Üsküdar glitt, ist die bekannteste und am wenigsten belegbare Geschichte des Turms. Die Genuesen errichteten den Turm 1348 am höchsten Punkt ihrer eigenen Mauern und nannten ihn Christusturm. Unter den Osmanen war er ein Feuerwachturm – in einer Stadt aus Holz wurde von hier aus Alarm geschlagen.

items.text: Генуэзцы, получившие от Византии свою колонию в Галате, увенчали её стены этой башней в 1348 году и назвали её Башней Христа. При османах она служила тюрьмой, обсерваторией и пожарной каланчой. Её навершие несколько раз менялось после пожаров и землетрясений; нынешний конус появился в ходе реставрации двадцатого века.

items.text: Ankara'dasınız, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk'ün anıtmezarı Anıtkabir'de. 1944-1953 yılları arasında yükselen bu anıtta yol, sizi Aslanlı Yol'dan tören meydanına çıkarır. Tasarım, Anadolu'nun Hitit ve Selçuklu mimarisinden aldığı biçimleri sade bir taş diliyle birleştirir. Anıtkabir sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz.

items.text: Atatürk 1938'de hayatını kaybettiğinde, onun için uluslararası bir yarışma açıldı. Yarışmayı Emin Onat ve Orhan Arda'nın projesi kazandı. Yapı, Ankara'ya hâkim Rasattepe'de 1944-1953 arasında inşa edildi. Hitit aslanlarından Selçuklu taş işçiliğine uzanan biçimler, burada sade bir anıt diline indirgendi. Ve 10 Kasım 1953'te Atatürk'ün naaşı buraya nakledildi.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Tören Meydanı'nın taşları ülkenin dört bir yanından getirildi. Anıtın yeri Ankara'ya hâkim Rasattepe'ydi ve inşaat sürerken tepenin altından Frig dönemine ait tümülüsler gün yüzüne çıktı.

items.text: You are at Anıtkabir, in Ankara province, built in 1944–1953: the mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. As you follow the Lion Road climbing to the ceremonial court, notice how Hittite and Seljuk forms are drawn into a deliberately plain language of stone.
items.speech: You are at Anıtkabir, in Ankara province, built in 1944 to 1953: the mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. As you follow the Lion Road climbing to the ceremonial court, notice how Hittite and Seljuk forms are drawn into a deliberately plain language of stone.

items.text: After Atatürk's death in 1938, an international competition was opened, and Emin Onat and Orhan Arda won it. Built between 1944 and 1953 on Rasattepe above Ankara, the monument reduces forms drawn from Hittite lions to Seljuk stonework into a deliberately plain monumental language. On 10 November 1953, Atatürk was moved here.

items.text: Did you know? The stone of the ceremonial plaza was brought from every part of the country, and the twenty-four lions of the Lion Road are carved seated, in the Hittite manner. The monument stands on Rasattepe above Ankara, and the building work uncovered Phrygian tumuli beneath the hill.

items.text: Above you rises Alanya Castle, a castle and walls in Antalya province, from the 13th century. This Seljuk fortress wraps the whole peninsula in 6.5 kilometres of wall. Below it, the shipyard and the Red Tower survive from the years when the city was a naval base.
items.speech: Above you rises Alanya Castle, a castle and walls in Antalya province, from the 13th century. This Seljuk fortress wraps the whole peninsula in 6.5 kilometres of wall. Below it, the shipyard and the Red Tower survive from the years when the city was a naval base.

items.text: In 1221 Alâeddin Keykubad I took the town and made it the Seljuk state's winter seat on the Mediterranean. Then the building began. The 6.5 kilometres of wall around the peninsula went up with more than a hundred towers and hundreds of cisterns. The shipyard below and the Red Tower belong to the years when the navy was built here.

items.text: As you wander, don't miss the Red Tower and the Shipyard, then climb on to the Inner citadel, the Süleymaniye Mosque and the Arsenal.
items.speech: As you wander, don't miss the Red Tower and the Shipyard, then climb on to the Inner citadel, the Süleymaniye Mosque and the Arsenal.

items.text: Did you know? The five-bay shipyard is the only one the Seljuks built on the Mediterranean coast, and it is still standing eight centuries on. The wall around the peninsula runs 6.5 kilometres and encloses hundreds of cisterns, so under siege the castle collected its own water. And the Red Tower, built to protect the Seljuk shipyard, is the best preserved tower of Anatolian Seljuk military architecture.

items.text: This is Maiden's Castle, in Mersin province, a sea castle of the 12th century rising from an islet two hundred metres offshore. It closed the harbour from one side, while Korykos Castle on the mainland closed the other: two guardians facing each other across the water.
items.speech: This is Maiden's Castle, in Mersin province, a sea castle of the 12th century rising from an islet two hundred metres offshore. It closed the harbour from one side, while Korykos Castle on the mainland closed the other: two guardians facing each other across the water.

items.text: The island castle was raised in the twelfth century under Byzantium. Later it passed to the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, and then to the Karamanids. Between it and Korykos Castle on the shore, a chain could be drawn to close the harbour mouth. And the name? It comes from a tale: a king's daughter was shut up here to keep her from a prophesied snakebite.

items.text: Did you know? The water between the two castles is shallow, and in summer, swimmers making for the island are the most familiar sight of this coast. The castle covers the whole islet, two hundred metres offshore, holding one side of the harbour while Korykos Castle held the other. And its name comes from the story of a king's daughter, shut up here to keep her from a prophesied snakebite.

items.text: Climb the slope where Eskişehir began, and you enter Odunpazarı Houses, a historic town of the 18th–19th century in Eskişehir province. This is the Ottoman quarter: timber houses corbelled out over narrow lanes, and inside them the city's meerschaum carvers still at work.

items.text: The quarter on the slope where Eskişehir began takes its name from the firewood market once held here. Look up at its timber-framed houses of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: they corbel out over the lane, each upper floor wider than the one below. And the meerschaum seams of the region made this quarter the centre of the pipe and carving workshops.

items.text: Did you know? Meerschaum is mined in only a few places on earth, and the finest comes from Eskişehir. It is carved while still soft from the ground, then hardens as it dries. Notice too that the upper floors are wider than the lower ones: the bays corbel out over the lane and win extra rooms from a narrow plot. And the quarter is home to the pipe and carving workshops fed by the Eskişehir seams, which produce the finest meerschaum in the world.

items.text: Here in Amasya province, along the Yeşilırmak, stand the Amasya Riverside Houses, from the 18th–19th century. A row of bow-fronted Ottoman houses lines the river, the rock tombs of the Pontic kings are cut into the cliff behind them, and the citadel hangs above.
